subject: MAP & Eval Plan: performance gating and staged close timeline
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Avery Brown <avery.brown@stellahealth.com>, Purchasing Team <purchasing@stellahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Subject: MAP & Eval Plan: performance gating and staged close timeline

Hi Avery / Stella procurement,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to get the MAP underway so we can validate performance at scale and lock the close timeline. I attached a first-pass MAP (stella_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a minimal test harness config (test_harness_config.yaml). Key asks and proposals below: 

1) Evaluation environment and scope
- Redwood-managed dedicated pool in us-west2 (replicates your target infra).
- Primary metrics: p95 latency (512-token generation), sustained throughput (QPS), TTFT (time-to-first-token), and effective concurrency under steady-state load.

2) Performance targets (initial gating suggestions)
- p95 latency <= 180 ms for 512-token responses (primary)
- Sustained throughput: 30 QPS (typical request mix)
- TTFT < 120 ms on warm instances
- Concurrency baseline: 32 sessions; target 64 for GA scale

3) Model variants to include in the MAP benchmark
- rwd-mixtral-8x-8bit (balanced quality / perf)
- rwd-llama-70b-8bit (higher quality, higher resource)
- rwd-mistral-7b-quant (fast, lower cost)
- a smaller fallback (rwd-alto-4b) for latency-critical flows

4) Quality evaluation plan
- Redwood will run a 1k-prompt sample derived from your anonymized FAQ and support transcripts (we'll provide a sampling script).
- Metrics: structured-field extraction F1, response correctness (binary), and human-preference blind A/B on 200 cases.

5) Schedule and next steps
- Kick-off: propose Tue 2026-06-22 for a 30-min MAP alignment call.
- Redwood to deliver two benchmark runs (canary + full) and a results memo by 2026-06-29.

Please confirm your acceptance criteria (especially p95 and concurrency) and whether the proposed GA target of early Aug works for procurement. Once we have acceptance tests from your side we can lock the canary timeline.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Strategic Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Lauren / team,

- Timeline: our business deadline is GA by 2026-08-01. Procurement needs a clear rollout plan and the MAP to show owners and deliverables to approve timeline.

Subject: RE: MAP & Eval Plan: performance gating and staged close timeline

Thanks — quick technical note on Redwood's planned benchmark runs and pass/fail rules so we can finalize the MAP owners table: 

1) Test harness and load profile
- Load driver: k6 for open-loop QPS tests + a synthetic convo driver for cold-start TTFT checks.
- Tokenization: use customer tokenizer mapping (we'll sync on exact vocab).
- Two baseline runs: (a) canary (5% traffic, 30min steady-state), (b) full-benchmark (100% simulated traffic mix, 2hr run).

2) Metrics and gating (automated)
- p95 latency (512 tokens) measured at service edge; pass = <= target threshold provided by customer (we'll test against both 180ms and 200ms).
- TTFT measured from request accept to first token delivered; pass = within threshold.
- Throughput: sustained QPS with error rate < 0.5%.
- Concurrency: validated by increasing virtual sessions until throughput degrades 10% from steady-state.

3) Quality tradeoffs and expected outcomes
- Mixtral-7b-quant: fastest (lowest TTFT), lower raw ROUGE on long-form; cost estimate: ~40% lower per-token cost vs 70b variant.
- Llama-70b-8bit: best quality for out-of-distribution medical questions, higher memory and slightly higher p95.
- Mixtral-8x-8bit: pragmatic midpoint; we expect ~10-15% higher latency than the 7b-quant but noticeably better correctness on structured responses.

4) Acceptance rule for quality
- Automated checks: structured-field extraction F1 >= 0.88 on the 1k set + human-review pass-rate >= 85% on 200 blind checks. If quality fails but perf passes, recommend model variant tiering (route latency-critical requests to 7b-quant, quality-critical to 70b).

5) Deliverables and owners (draft)
- Redwood: benchmark runs + results memo (Rishi) by 2026-06-29; canary monitoring dashboard (Priyom) during rollout.
- Stella: acceptance test set + procurement checklist by 2026-06-21.

I'm attaching a compact benchmark matrix with expected resource footprints per variant (benchmark_matrix_q1.csv). Will adjust thresholds once Stella shares their prompt set.

-rishi
Principal ML Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

All — thanks for the quick responses and alignment. Finalized MAP summary below and next steps (I updated the attached MAP worksheet):

Kick-off / cadence
- Kick-off: Tue 2026-06-22 10:00 AM PT (30 min) — agenda: scope, acceptance tests, data handoff.
- Weekly syncs: Tuesdays 10:00 AM PT (standing) until GA.

Key deliverables and owners
- Customer: acceptance test set + procurement checklist (Stella) by 2026-06-21.
- Redwood: two benchmark runs + results memo (Rishi) by 2026-06-29; monitoring dashboard and canary run owner (Priyom).
- Redwood CS / Solutions: run the human-preference A/B and coordinate the 200-case blind review (Karthik).

Rollout plan (staged)
- Canary: 5% traffic (duration 1 day validation, 30m steady-state)
- Ramp: 25% -> 75% over 1 week, monitor cost/latency tradeoffs
- GA: full traffic after acceptance sign-off (target 2026-08-01)

Benchmarks Redwood will publish
- Perf memo: p50/p95/p99, TTFT, QPS, error rate, effective concurrency thresholds per model variant.
- Cost delta: $/1M tokens est for each variant (we'll include reserved capacity vs burst cost estimates).

Next steps
- Avery: confirm procurement contact has what they need and confirm kick-off time.
- Stella: drop the acceptance prompt set into the shared Drive link by Mon 2026-06-21.
- Redwood: run canary + full benchmark and share memo by Tue 2026-06-29.

Looking forward — we'll use the MAP worksheet to keep owners and dates updated.

Regards,
